nodes.label: Identifying key legal facts in a scenario
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Identify the material facts within a factual scenario from which legal issues arise.
essentialPoints: Distinguish legally relevant facts from background/irrelevant detail
Material facts trigger specific legal rules or elements of an offence/tort
Accurate fact identification is the starting point for all legal analysis
specRefs: Analyse a factual scenario by identifying the key facts from which legal issues arise

nodes.label: Identifying the legal issue(s) raised by facts
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Formulate the precise legal question(s) that the identified facts give rise to.
essentialPoints: Convert material facts into a legal question capable of being answered by a rule
A scenario may raise multiple distinct issues requiring separate analysis
specRefs: Analyse a factual scenario by identifying the key facts from which legal issues arise

nodes.label: Literal rule of statutory interpretation
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the literal rule by giving words in a statute their plain, ordinary meaning.
essentialPoints: Words given their plain, grammatical, ordinary meaning even if the result is absurd
Example: Whiteley v Chappell / LNER v Berriman illustrate literal approach
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Golden rule of statutory interpretation
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the golden rule to modify literal wording where it would produce an absurd result.
essentialPoints: Narrow application: choose between two possible literal meanings
Wide application: modify wording to avoid an absurd or repugnant outcome (e.g. Re Sigsworth)
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Mischief rule of statutory interpretation
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the mischief rule by interpreting a statute to remedy the mischief Parliament intended to address (Heydon's Case).
essentialPoints: Look at the gap/mischief in the law before the statute and interpret to suppress it
Example: Smith v Hughes
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Purposive approach to statutory interpretation
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the purposive approach by interpreting a statute in light of Parliament's underlying purpose, including using extraneous aids.
essentialPoints: Broader than mischief rule: asks what Parliament intended the Act to achieve overall
Example: Jones v Tower Boot Co; influenced by EU-derived and human-rights interpretation duties
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Intrinsic and extrinsic aids to interpretation
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Use intrinsic aids (within the Act) and extrinsic aids (outside the Act, e.g. Hansard per Pepper v Hart) to support statutory interpretation.
essentialPoints: Intrinsic aids: long/short title, preamble, schedules, definition sections
Extrinsic aids: dictionaries, Hansard (Pepper v Hart), explanatory notes, prior case law
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Rules of language (ejusdem generis, expressio unius, noscitur a sociis)
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the linguistic canons of construction to interpret ambiguous statutory wording.
essentialPoints: Ejusdem generis: general words following specific words are limited to the same class
Expressio unius est exclusio alterius: express mention of one thing excludes others
Noscitur a sociis: a word is known by the company it keeps
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Applying statutory interpretation rules to resolve a scenario
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Select and apply the appropriate approach(es) to statutory interpretation to determine how a statute applies to a given scenario.
essentialPoints: Different rules can produce different outcomes for the same wording
Justify choice of approach by reference to statutory wording and context
specRefs: Analyse legislation by applying the rules and principles of statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Ratio decidendi as the binding element of a precedent
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Identify the ratio decidendi of a case as the legal reasoning that binds future courts.
essentialPoints: Ratio decidendi is the reason for the decision, binding in later cases
Distinguished from obiter dicta, which is persuasive only
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Obiter dicta as persuasive precedent
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Identify obiter dicta as statements not forming part of the ratio, which are persuasive but not binding.
essentialPoints: Comments made 'by the way', not necessary to the decision
May be followed by later courts but carry no binding force
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Court hierarchy and binding precedent
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Explain how the doctrine of stare decisis operates through the hierarchy of courts, so lower courts are bound by higher courts.
essentialPoints: Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, High Court, lower courts each bind those below
Supreme Court can depart from its own past decisions (Practice Statement 1966); Court of Appeal generally bound by own decisions subject to Young v Bristol Aeroplane exceptions
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Distinguishing a precedent
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply the technique of distinguishing to avoid an otherwise binding precedent by identifying material differences in facts.
essentialPoints: A court avoids following a precedent by showing the facts are materially different
Allows courts flexibility without overruling the earlier case
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Overruling and reversing precedent
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Distinguish overruling (a later, different case changes the law stated in an earlier case) from reversing (same case, on appeal).
essentialPoints: Overruling: higher court in a later, separate case departs from an earlier decision
Reversing: appellate court changes the decision of a lower court in the same case
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Applying the doctrine of precedent to a scenario
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Use identification of ratio, obiter, court hierarchy and techniques of avoidance to determine which precedent governs a given scenario.
essentialPoints: Locate the relevant binding authority from the court hierarchy
Assess whether it can be distinguished, or whether it has been overruled
specRefs: Analyse case law by applying the doctrine of precedent

nodes.label: Breaking legal rules into constituent elements
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Decompose a legal rule or test into its individual constituent elements before applying each in turn.
essentialPoints: Legal rules (offences, torts, defences) are composed of separate elements each requiring proof
Systematic breakdown prevents missing a required element
specRefs: Analyse, apply and evaluate the legal rules and principles of each area of law: break them into constituent parts and apply them to a hypothetical scenario

nodes.label: Applying legal rules to a hypothetical scenario
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Apply each constituent element of a legal rule methodically to the facts of a hypothetical scenario to reach a reasoned conclusion.
essentialPoints: Match facts to each element in turn, supporting each match with authority
Reach a supported conclusion on whether the rule is satisfied
specRefs: Analyse, apply and evaluate the legal rules and principles of each area of law: break them into constituent parts and apply them to a hypothetical scenario

nodes.label: Evaluating legal rules and principles
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Evaluate the strengths, weaknesses and possible reform of a legal rule after applying it to a scenario.
essentialPoints: Evaluation goes beyond description to assess fairness, clarity, consistency or need for reform
Grounded in applied outcome, not abstract rule alone
specRefs: Analyse, apply and evaluate the legal rules and principles of each area of law: break them into constituent parts and apply them to a hypothetical scenario

nodes.label: Structuring a clear, logical legal argument
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Construct a legal argument with a clear logical structure moving from issue to rule to application to conclusion.
essentialPoints: Follows an issue-rule-application-conclusion structure
Each step follows logically from the last, avoiding unsupported leaps
specRefs: Construct clear, concise and logical legal arguments substantiated by legal authority, using appropriate legal terminology

nodes.label: Substantiating arguments with legal authority
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Support every legal assertion made in an argument with an appropriate statutory provision or case authority.
essentialPoints: Every rule stated should be backed by a case or statute
Authority must be relevant and correctly applied, not merely cited
specRefs: Construct clear, concise and logical legal arguments substantiated by legal authority, using appropriate legal terminology

nodes.label: Using appropriate legal terminology
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Use precise and correct legal terminology when constructing legal arguments.
essentialPoints: Correct technical vocabulary (e.g. 'ratio', 'mens rea', 'claimant') improves precision and credibility
Imprecise or lay language can obscure or misstate the legal point
specRefs: Construct clear, concise and logical legal arguments substantiated by legal authority, using appropriate legal terminology

nodes.label: Writing concisely in legal argument
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Express legal arguments concisely, avoiding irrelevant material and unnecessary repetition.
essentialPoints: Focus only on facts and rules relevant to the identified issue
Concision aids clarity and effective use of time in an exam response
specRefs: Construct clear, concise and logical legal arguments substantiated by legal authority, using appropriate legal terminology

nodes.label: Arguing by analogy where precedent is absent or conflicting
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Construct a persuasive legal argument in a novel scenario by reasoning from analogous authority where no clear or consistent precedent exists.
essentialPoints: Identify the closest analogous case(s) or underlying principle to extend by analogy
Address conflicting lines of authority and justify which should be preferred
Argument's persuasiveness rests on coherence with existing legal principle, not just assertion
specRefs: Construct a persuasive argument where there are no clear or conflicting precedents

nodes.label: Identifying different legal perspectives on an issue
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Identify the range of differing viewpoints or arguable positions that arise on a contested legal issue.
essentialPoints: Recognise that a legal issue may have more than one reasonably arguable answer
Consider viewpoints of different parties or schools of legal thought
specRefs: Analyse and critically evaluate legal issues by identifying different perspectives, supporting the strongest viewpoint and countering alternatives

nodes.label: Supporting the strongest viewpoint with reasoned justification
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Select and justify the most defensible viewpoint on a contested legal issue using authority and reasoning.
essentialPoints: Weigh the identified perspectives against strength of supporting authority and principle
Present a clear, justified conclusion favouring one viewpoint
specRefs: Analyse and critically evaluate legal issues by identifying different perspectives, supporting the strongest viewpoint and countering alternatives

nodes.label: Countering alternative viewpoints
nodes.theme: Theme 0 - Legal skills: analysing scenarios, applying authority and building arguments
nodes.objective: Anticipate and rebut alternative viewpoints to strengthen the overall persuasiveness of a legal argument.
essentialPoints: Directly address weaknesses in opposing arguments rather than ignoring them
Rebuttal should use authority or logical reasoning, not mere assertion
specRefs: Analyse and critically evaluate legal issues by identifying different perspectives, supporting the strongest viewpoint and countering alternatives
